title: PSG, Morocco defender Achraf Hakimi set to face trial after rape allegation
content:
Paris Saint-Germain defender Achraf Hakimi has said he will face trial following an allegation of rape.

Hakimi, who also plays for the Morocco national team, said in a statement posted on X that he denied the accusation against him.

“Today, a rape accusation is enough to justify a trial, even though I deny it and everything proves it’s false,” he wrote on X. “This is as unjust to the innocent as it is to the genuine victims. I calmly await this trial, which will allow the truth to come out publicly.”

The accusation relates to an incident alleged to have occurred in February 2023, when a 24-year-old woman claimed Hakimi assaulted her, The Athletic previously reported, citing multiple reports in the French media.

Hakimi was charged in March 2023. He has always denied any wrongdoing.

Fanny Colin, Hakimi’s lawyer, said in a statement, shared with The Athletic: “We are determined and ready to fight as we await this trial so that justice may be served.” She told The Athletic she had appealed against the decision.

The Athletic has contacted the Nanterre public prosecutor’s office for further details.

The plaintiff’s lawyer, Rachel-Flore Pardo, told the Associated Press her client welcomed the decision to send the case to trial “with relief,” adding that it is “fully consistent with the evidence in the file.”

In a statement, shared with the Associated Press, she added: “There are still circles where the MeToo movement has not broken the sound barrier, with the world of men’s football at the forefront.”

PSG play Monaco at the Parc des Princes in the Champions League in the round of 32 on Wednesday. They won the first leg 3-2.

Hakimi started PSG’s last match, a 3-0 victory over Metz on Saturday.

Asked about the 27-year-old’s involvement at a press conference today ahead of the Monaco game, Luis Enrique told reporters: “This is in the hands of the justice system.”

Hakimi was part of the Morocco squad that reached the final of the Africa Cup of Nations on home soil, losing to Senegal in a dramatic final. Morocco have qualified for the World Cup and are in Group C with Brazil, Scotland and Haiti.

The Athletic has contacted PSG for a response.

A date for the trial hasn’t been fixed yet.
